item.title: From theory to pitch: CBF, CONMEBOL and Pernambuco FA train academy staff
item.description: From theory to pitch: CBF, CONMEBOL and Pernambuco FA train academy staff The CBF, CONMEBOL Evolución and the Pernambuco Football Federation (FPF) brought a youth football training program to Recife. From October 20 to 22, 40 professionals from 27 different institutions attended the seminar, led by Wilton Santana and PC de Oliveira at Retrô’s training center. The three-day program combined theoretical classes and practical activities, covering topics such as the coach’s role in developing players, differences in training approaches and leadership in the development process, activity planning and the application of tactical principles. The first two days focused on theory, covering topics such as the coach’s role in developing players Credits: Rafael Vieira / FPF Participants came from a variety of backgrounds, including coaches, assistant coaches, coordinators, supervisors and club officials. The program also welcomed representatives from the state’s leading clubs, including Sport, Santa Cruz, Náutico, Retrô, Belo Jardim, Carpinense and Chã Grande On the first two days, participants attended classes in the morning and early afternoon, followed by on-field activities with players from Retrô’s Under-12/13 and Under-15/17 teams. On the final day, participants put their newly acquired knowledge into practice on the pitch during activities with Retrô’s youth teams Credits: Rafael Vieira / FPF On the final day, the format was reversed: participants themselves led drills with the Under-14 and Under-15 teams under the instructors’ supervision. This was followed by technical feedback and the presentation of certificates. For Pernambuco Football Federation president Evandro Carvalho, the initiative offers great prospects for the clubs’ future by enhancing professionals’ skills and strengthening youth development. “Investing in professional training means investing in the future of football. Closer ties between the FPF, the CBF and CONMEBOL help expand access to knowledge and working methods, ensuring our clubs are increasingly well equipped to develop young players. Pernambuco has an important role in this process, and hosting an initiative like this reinforces our commitment to the growth of football at every stage,” he told the FPF website. item.title: Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing set for golden opportunity they might not get again
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jordan Watkins #17 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball during an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the 49ers take the sensible, long-term approach, then they will not have Mike Evans available for their Week 7 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons after his Achilles issue flared up in their Monday Night Football win over the Washington Commanders. San Francisco is shorn of wide receiver depth due to a remarkable cluster of injuries at the position, and the 49er passing game was ineffective without Evans after he left the game against the Commanders. Evans has developed a superb rapport with Brock Purdy, serving as a devastatingly effective easy button for the San Francisco quarterback. The future Hall of Famer’s connection with Purdy is likely to be critical down the stretch and in the postseason as the 49ers aim to realize their Super Bowl aspirations and, as such, there is little reason for San Francisco to risk a serious injury to Evans by pushing him to play against the Falcons when they are 6-0 with a three-game lead in the NFC West. Though the 49ers look likely to be without Evans, they could get a boost with the return of Christian Kirk from the calf issue that has kept him out for the entire season to this point. But it is perhaps a tad ambitious to expert Kirk to hit the ground running right off the bat and, in Evans’ potential absence, the passing game will most likely predominantly go through tight end George Kittle. Yet the dearth of other options would also leave the Falcons game as a golden opportunity for Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing to impress and stake a claim for a larger amount of offensive snaps going forward. Both Cowing (2024) and Watkins (2025) came into the league as fourth-round picks with skill sets that suggested they could be dynamic options in the Kyle Shanahan offense. Yet their potential in that regard has remained largely untapped. Cowing and Watkins each displayed speed and route-running craft in college that figured to translate well to the NFL level. Both Cowing (2024) and Watkins (2025) came into the league as fourth-round picks with skill sets that suggested they could be dynamic options in the Kyle Shanahan offense. Yet their potential in that regard has remained largely untapped. Cowing and Watkins each displayed speed and route-running craft in college that figured to translate well to the NFL level. However, they have each seen injuries check their progress. After playing only a peripheral role in 2024, Cowing lost an entire season to injury in 2025, when a preseason high-ankle sprain curtailed the ascent Watkins was seemingly enjoying as a rookie. Heading into Week 7, Cowing and Watkins each have just five catches each in their respective careers. Cowing has only 89 yards to his name, while Watkins has 108, with the former seemingly on thin ice in his role as a return man having muffed a punt in the win over the Seattle Seahawks before making an ill-advised decision to return one from the four-yard line in the defeat of the Commanders. After Evans again missed practice on Thursday, it seems highly likely Watkins and Cowing will have prominent roles to play regardless of Kirk’s involvement. Even with Christian Kirk probably returning on Sunday, Watkins should have a decent role to play. Nice work here recovering from the stumble on the incidental contact, working back to the ball and then managing to get upfield for YAC. pic.twitter.com/JqseP6Piwo — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 22, 2026 It is an opportunity neither can afford to waste, as they may not get another this season. While Evans’ Achilles issue will need to be managed throughout the year, he will be expected to return in Week 9 if he does indeed miss the Falcons game. Deebo Samuel is also expected back after the bye, though rookie De’Zhaun Stribling will have to wait a little longer to make his return from the ankle injury suffered in the season opener. In other words, they will each be down the pecking order again soon. From Watkins at least, there have been some encouraging flashes of promise this season, the former Ole Miss wideout making catches of 34 and 26 yards in the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals and doing an excellent job overcoming physical coverage to make a 22-yard reception against the Commanders. Nothing spectacular here, but Jordan Watkins has played 45% of the offensive snaps this season. Injuries aside, some of that will be tied to the fact that he's shown buy-in as a run-blocker, including on the weird inadvertent Kaelon Black direct snap play. pic.twitter.com/LSeeyvhr5y — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 22, 2026 Watkins has also displayed admirable commitment as a run blocker this season, with his effort in that area of the game likely a reason why he has been trusted to play 45 percent of the offensive snaps so far in 2026. Asked why Watkins hasn’t had more targets, quarterback Brock Purdy replied on Thursday: “Honestly, it has nothing to do with not trying to get him the ball or anything. I think that’s just sort of how the game’s gone. He’s definitely a playmaker. He’s done that since he’s got here. And it’s just been tough with him getting opportunities when we have like [WR] Mike Evans, [WR] Demarcus Robinson, [TE] George [Kittle], [RB] Christian [McCaffrey], like other guys too and he’s trying to get in that mix. But, he’s been consistent. He’s been a guy that has stayed faithful to this whole process. And now he’s getting a shot and opportunity. So, I feel like we will over time. Hopefully this game too, I can get him the ball. Watching the film, that’s definitely a guy that I’m like, ‘Yeah, I’d love to get the ball to him.’ He’s shown flashes and glimpses of not even just catching the ball, but making plays after the catch too or getting YAC after the catch. So, I feel you on that and that’s something that I watch and I want to have our connection get better and better, but has nothing to do with not trying to give him the ball or anything like that.” Of the two, Watkins seems the more likely to have success in carving out a long-term role in the offense. Cowing was put the behind the 8-ball by his lost 2025 and has not caught up, with his stock at a low ebb amid his questionable performance as a returner. But if either is going to have a compelling case for being involved in the offense once the likes of Evans and Samuel return, then they need to make the most of the chance that looks set to come their way on Sunday. There is concern about how the 49er passing game will look without Evans in Atlanta. If either Cowing or Watkins can ensure it still succeeds, then it would serve as a great boost to their long-term prospects and the depth of the 49er receiving corps.

item.description: Look, it’s Kayl Petersen defending Noelle Anthon in the same picture, how helpful. | Credit: Marquette University It’s time to continue our 2026-27 season preview for Marquette women’s basketball! We’re moving forward with our look at head coach Cara Consuegra’s roster for this year. We’ve already rummaged around in what to expect from Halle Vice , and peeked under the hood at who else is returning from last year’s roster . Go give those a click to get caught up on things if you haven’t already, and heck, wander around in our entire season preview package if you haven’t done that, too. Today we’re looking at the five transfers on the Marquette roster right now. There’s four that have made their way to Milwaukee from a Division 1 team and one from the junior college ranks. We’ll go through them in order of Division 1 experience, although that’s obviously not going to be sorted by post-high school experience, if that makes sense. Anyway, off we go, starting off with the player on the roster who already has some experience playing in the Big East….. MacKenzie Givens Junior — #12 — Guard — 6’0” — Cincinnati, Ohio MacKenzie Givens comes to Marquette after two seasons at Xavier. This is literally leaving a hometown team for her, so that seems like kind of a big deal. She played just 139 total minutes as a freshman for the Musketeers as they went 7-24 under the direction of Billi Chambers, but Givens was a most-of-the-time starter for Xavier this past season. She got the nod in 24 of her 29 appearances, missing a road trip to Providence in early February. She was coming off the bench to start the season but then was in the first five the rest of the way after that. Givens was Xavier’s #2 scorer at 11.7 points per game, and she chipped in 4.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals as well. BartTorvik.com has Givens as the most productive player on Xavier’s roster last season, rating the best both in terms of how efficient she was in her usage and points above average. She was also the only Musketeer with an offensive rating north of 90, and she was waaaaay up there at 106.6. Her Hoop Stats has her in the top 500 in the country in offensive rating and top 400 in turnover rate. In other words: If you were going to swipe one person off a roster that went 11-19 overall and 4-16 in the Big East, you could do a lot worse than Givens. In terms of immediate obvious fit for Marquette, at worst Givens is a reliable backcourt option. I wouldn’t be shocked to see her start on opening night at either the 2 or the 3, depending on how head coach Cara Consuegra considers the talents of Jordan Meulemans relative to the positions on the floor. If Givens can keep developing her three-point shot — she hit less than 32% last season — that will pay dividends for the Golden Eagles. With Halle Vice being the only player that has an obvious set role, the sky’s the limit for what Givens could contribute. The only question we have to ask is: If she was capable of a lot more, why didn’t we see it

Kayl Petersen Junior — #34 — Forward — 6’1” — Waupun, Wisconsin Finally, this November, we will get to see Kayl Petersen debut in a Marquette uniform. She was originally set to join the Golden Eagles in the fall of 2024, but the coaching change led her to follow Megan Duffy to Virginia Tech. That worked out decently well for Petersen in Year 1, averaging just under 16 minutes a game mostly off the bench and adding 4.2 points and 2.9 rebounds as the Hokies went 19-13, but missed the NCAA tournament. Year #2, not so hot for Petersen, as she played in all but one game, but her minutes fell to just under 11 per game. She was a little less productive in general as a result, perhaps as a result of not quite getting in rhythm in her reduced role. VaTech went 23-10 last year and got to the NCAA tournament, so it’s hard to judge Duffy’s roster management here…. but you can see why Petersen perhaps went looking for an option with a little bit more playing time available to her. At 6’1”, perhaps Petersen doesn’t immediately showcase as an obvious productive force inside, but the fact of the matter is that she has a career rebounding rate of 8.8 per 40 minutes, and she was north of 10 per 40 minutes this past season. Her Hoop Stats ranks her top 500 in the country on the glass on both ends of the floor, and she was just barely outside the top 250 in the country in defensive win shares per 40 minutes last season. If all she does is body people inside and clean the glass, that’s okay by me. If she’s going to pull in nearly four offensive rebounds per 40 minutes of action like she did last year, Petersen’s going to have to do better than shooting 43% on two-pointers, though. Yu Han Lin Sophomore — #11 — Guard — 5’9” — Hualien, Taiwan The thing we have to unlock about Yu Han Lin when it comes to figuring out what she can bring to Marquette this season is answering the question as to why she started in seven of Middle Tennessee’s first 11 games, then not at all the rest of the season. Then as a secondary question, we have to figure out why Lin played at least 14 minutes in all seven games that she started and averaged over 23 minutes in those games … but then just over 11 minutes in her 26 games off the bench. That includes 14 games where she played single digit minutes, and 10 games where she played less than five minutes. That includes single digit outings in each of MTSU’s last six games of the year. I think all of that explains why she’s not at Middle Tennessee any more, it’s just not particularly encouraging for what it means for her ability to play at Marquette in the Big East. Middle Tennessee went 17-16 last season with an 11-7 record in Conference USA. Head coach Rick Insell is far from a goof, last year broke a run of four straight 26+ win seasons, and he’s gotten to at least 20 wins in 18 of his seasons with the Blue Raiders dating back to 2005-06. He’s been to the NCAA tournament 12 times with MTSU, but there’s something about Lin that said “okay, gotta play her” and then something that said “oh, no, can’t play her at all” even while the season wasn’t bending towards a more typical season for him. As a starter, Yu Han Lin averaged 9.0 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game last season. She was great inside the arc, shooting 58% on twos, but she shot 1-for-16 from behind the three-point line. Off the bench, she averaged just 3.5 points plus an assist and a rebound per game. She was suddenly not good inside the arc at just 40%, but suddenly she found a shooting touch, going 9-for-25, which is 36% which is absolutely fine by me. From a deeper analytical level, she had a tremendous assist rate according to Her Hoop Stats , ranking #314 in the country. That’s great, especially as Marquette clearly needs a point guard. However, her nearly 28% turnover rate was somewhere in the bottom third of the entire country, maybe worse since not every player on every team would have had the minutes to qualify for the rankings. Is that why Lin couldn’t play regularly for the Blue Raiders? Her 34 turnovers in her first 11 games with Middle Tennessee? And if that is the problem, what’s going to change about how she plays when she goes from Conference USA to the Big East to stop that problem from reoccurring… or even getting worse? Brooklyn Hall Redshirt Freshman — #1 — Guard — 6’1” — Dayton, Ohio Brooklyn Hall gets to be Not Last in this list because she spent half a season on a Division 1 roster last year. She was a spring semester enrollee at South Florida last January, but then she hit the transfer portal since USF elected to not keep on their interim head coach after Jose Fernandez left to coach the Dallas Wings in the WNBA. One Marquette hire of Sheila Boykin as an assistant coach later, and Hall is a Golden Eagle now instead of a Bull. item.title: Purdue Baseball invites fans to annual Halloween bash
item.description: Purdue Baseball is bringing costumes and trick-or-treating onto the field for its annual Halloween Bash at Alexander Field on Oct. 28. The free, all-ages event begins at 6 p.m., according to a community announcement. Players will dress up for a brief costume scrimmage before children take the field to trick-or-treat with players and coaches. Azzip Pizza is returning as the event's official sponsor for the second year. Fans are also encouraged to attend in costume. The event date could change if the forecast indicates another evening would offer more favorable weather. Fans can get a free Purdue Baseball ticket Everyone attending the Halloween Bash will receive a voucher redeemable for one free ticket to any regular-season Purdue Baseball home game during the 2027 season. Purdue has six home weekends plus several midweek dates scheduled at Alexander Field after winning 20 home games last season for the second time in team history. The Halloween Bash debuted at Alexander Field in 2019 and returned to the calendar in 2021. It has continued as an October event since then. More Purdue Baseball events are planned Purdue is also planning its First Pitch Dinner at the Ross-Ade Pavilion and its all-ages Preseason Fan Fest inside the Mollenkopf Athletic Center. Both events are held early in the spring semester. The Preseason Fan Fest generally takes place the weekend before college baseball’s national opening day, which is Feb. 19 this school year. item.title: North Shore gets a surprise visit from Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud
item.description: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud runs onto the field as he is introduced before an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) C.J. Stroud brought a little more star power to North Shore's preparations for one of its biggest games of the season . The Texans' quarterback visited the No. 2 state-ranked Mustangs as part of a Jordan Brand event ahead of Friday's matchup against No. 7 C.E. King at Galena Park ISD Stadium. A video shared by VYPE Houston on Wednesday morning captured a celebration that included custom apparel, music and Houston rapper Bun B's famous Trill Burgers. Stroud's entrance fit the occasion. The video shows a red slab rolling up to a gathering at the Mustangs' home stadium, with Stroud greeting the crowd as people surround the car and raise their phones to capture the moment. The festivities extended beyond the football team. Children and adults mingled outside, fans posed with North Shore apparel, and the school's Mustang mascot made an appearance. Inside the locker room, players showed off black clothing featuring North Shore's red-and-white logo. Other scenes highlighted a Nike-branded setup with the phrase "Proof is in the pressure" with shirts bearing the same message. VYPE's post identified Jordan Brand as the organizer of the visit. Stroud has his own connection to the Jumpman. He agreed to a multiyear endorsement deal with Jordan Brand in September 2024. Stroud's appearance added to the buildup for a game featuring two programs that played for state championships last season. item.title: Chase Elliott Removes Name From Most Popular Driver Ballot In Honor of Kyle Busch
item.description: On Friday, Chase Elliott showcased why he has become NASCAR’s most popular driver over the last eight seasons. The driver of the No. 9 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet has officially chosen to opt out of a chance to be crowned the most popular driver in the NASCAR Cup Series this season. The reason? To give Kyle Busch, who passed away in May, a clearer path to securing the award posthumously. Busch, who is featured on the ballot, has never taken home the NASCAR Most Popular Driver Award. If this gesture by Elliott feels eerily familiar, it’s because his father, Bill Elliott, also removed his name from the ballot in 2001, which paved the way for Dale Earnhardt, a seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion who was killed in a final lap crash of the Daytona 500 that season, to win the award for the only time in his Hall of Fame career. Bill Elliott won the NMPA Most Popular Driver Award a record 16 times. With Chase Elliott removing his name from the ballot, this means for the first time since Darrell Waltrip took home the award in 1990, there will be a driver not named Earnhardt or Elliott taking home the Most Popular Driver Award in the NASCAR Cup Series. Prior to the Coca-Cola 600 race weekend, Busch fell ill with a bout of sepsis and suddenly passed away at the age of 41. Busch, a two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion, was the winningest driver in the history of the NASCAR National Series, as he had racked up 234 victories between NASCAR’s three National Series divisions. Busch’s final NASCAR National Series win came at Dover Motor Speedway, a week prior to his unexpected death. Fans looking to vote for the 2026 Most Popular Driver are encouraged to visit the Most Popular Driver landing page . Fans can vote for one driver per ballot submission with voting being limited to five submissions per day, per email at NASCAR.com/mostpopulardriver or on the NASCAR Mobile App. The five votes per day aren’t limited to a single driver. item.title: Mainz 05 vs Werder Bremen Preview: Battle of the strikers
item.description: Mainz 05 vs Werder Bremen Preview: Battle of the strikers Mainz Mainz have started very strongly into the season and sit in fifth place after an away win against Schalke but they are yet to convince at home. Their start to the season has been hugely helped by one player - Phillip Tietz. The German striker has five goals from the first six league games and has scored in all but two this campaign. By contrast, Tietz now already has one less goal than he managed in the entire 2025-26 Bundesliga campaign on matchday seven. Mainz have the upper hand defensively against Saturday's opponent too as they have managed three clean sheets this campaign already. In spite of this, Werder Bremen will be comforted by the fact that when Mainz do concede the goals start pouring in. In the games during this campaign where Mainz has conceded, all their opponents have managed to score at least three goals against them in the Bundesliga. Mainz have only won once in their last five games against Werder Bremen with their last home win coming back in 2020. Mainz's secondary striker Sheraldo Becker has been the second fastest player this season in the Bundesliga with a top speed of 36.6 km/h. Ahead of the tie, Mainz coach Urs Fischer said: “The entire Bremen side makes a very strong impression. On three occasions they have been 2-0 down and they have come back.” Team news Dominik Kohr is out with an ankle injury alongside Otto Ruoppi and Silas who are also injured. Robin Zentner continues to be out with a hand issue and will be replaced by Alexander Schwolow. Werder Bremen With their third consecutive game coming from two goals down to grab a result, Werder Bremen drew 2-2 with Paderborn after being 2-0 down securing their status as the comeback kings. Helping out in this run has been the return to form of striker Niclas Füllkrug who is the Bundesliga's top scorer with six goals. His return to Werder Bremen on loan has helped to revive his career after leaving the club in 2023 to then have mixed spells at Dortmund (where he left after a year), West Ham and AC Milan on loan. However, it has not just been Füllkrug who has made Bremen's attack one to be feared this season as Marco Grüll has set up four goals and sits as the league's highest assister. Despite the attacking power, Bremen have been vulnerable at the back in conceding 12 goals and are yet to keep a clean sheet this season. Sitting in 8th place, they will leapfrog Mainz if they manage to grab all three points away from home on Saturday for the first time this Bundesliga season. Before the game, Bremen coach Daniel Thioune said: “Mainz defend a lot with a low block and are very physical and strong. We have to be at 100 percent.” Team news Felix Agu, Moussa N'Diaye, Jens Stage, Skelly Alvero, Salim Musah, Niklas Stark, Keke Topp and Justin Njinmah make for a lenghty injury list for Werder Bremen. Senne Lynen is also a doubt for the tie.

item.title: Bukayo Saka injury ‘not good’ as Arsenal face nervous wait
item.description: Arsenal are still yet to discover the extent of Bukayo Saka ’s thigh injury but Mikel Arteta has admitted the early signs are “not good”. The England international pulled up with the issue in the first half of the 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday. Saka is set to undergo further assessment ahead of Arsenal’s home match against Everton on Saturday. Bukayo Saka leaves the pitch after incurring an injury (Adam Davy/PA) (PA Wire) But he did not train on Friday and Arsenal face a nervous wait before discovering how long he could be sidelined for. The BBC reported that Saka could miss a minimum of six weeks, up to two months, with the quadriceps problem. “He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury,” Arteta said. "We will know more probably tomorrow. We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. "Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch and is struggling to walk without any pain and is restricted to movement, they are not good signs. “So let's be very patient so we can give a definitive assessment, and then let you know." Saka’s injury means Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze will have the opportunity to start against Everton. Madueke scored Arsenal’s winner at Nottingham Forest last Sunday while Eze was on target in the draw at the Allianz Arena in midweek. With forward Christos Tzolis also sidelined, Madueke and Eze will be given additional responsibility for leading Arsenal’s attack. Saka missed several stretches of the past two seasons due to a mixture of muscle injuries - dealing with hamstring, thigh and hip problems. Saka went down unopposed before limping off in Munich (Reuters) The 25-year-old was also affected by an Achilles injury over the final stretch of last season, which impacted his fitness at the summer’s World Cup. Arsenal play five times before the November international break and travel to Liverpool in the Premier League next weekend. Following Saturday’s home game against Everton, there are also trips to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup and Slavia Prague in the Champions League. They conclude the stretch of fixtures by hosting Hull in the Premier League on 7 November ahead of the two-week international window. A longer lay-off could rule Saka out of matches against Newcastle, Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham and Real Madrid after the break.

item.title: Locksley the first domino to fall; is anybody next?
item.description: Nov 30, 2019; East Lansing, MI, USA; Maryland Terrapins head coach Mike Locksley stands on the field during the second half against the Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mike Carter-USA TODAY Sports The 2026 football season was devoid of firings…until now There’s a Yiddish expression about jinxes and evil eyes. Kenahora is meant to ward off bad things. Sort of like, don’t say it and it won’t happen. Well, The Athletic said it , or wrote it, on October 16: Why haven’t any college football head coaches been fired yet this season? Boom! Mike Locksley is gone. We recently posted about a website we came across, Coaches Hotseat , that had Locksley as the hottest seat in the country. With his dismissal – or mutual separation – the top spot among hotseat coaches falls to No. 2, Greg Schiano. Although not everyone has GS as the heir apparent, at least from a betting perspective: It took seven weeks, but Mike Locksley is the first coach fired this season. The NEW odds for "next coach fired", Via @BetOnline_ag . DeBoer and Sark 75/1. pic.twitter.com/ZW4ikB3GH6 — Pat Smith (@patsmithradio) October 21, 2026 We are at the midpoint, more or less, of the season. And as the article in The Athletic points out, firing a coach, even for teams with the financial wherewithal, is not an easy call. According to agents, administrators and coaches who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the market candidly, many schools have finally reached a spending ceiling, leading them to rethink when to make changes and whether a change is really the solution. “It’s a combination of losing a roster and finding the budget to compete while also paying absurd buyouts,” one agent said. Money talks, and it often says, “Wait a minute!” The conversation seems to be about the cost-benefit aspect of firing a coach mid-season. Is it the coach? The roster? For Horcoff, acquiring a talented young center would address one of the organization’s most pressing long-term weaknesses. It would also give Detroit another potential building block to develop alongside players such as Lucas Raymond, Moritz Seider, and Alex DeBrincat. There is a downside to that approach, especially if it involves trading Larkin. A promising prospect might eventually develop into a top-line center, but Detroit would be surrendering a proven player capable of handling that responsibility right now. Dylan Larkin Trade Talks Could Become More Complicated Friedman’s report arrives as Detroit continues exploring its options involving Larkin, who requested a trade following last season. The 30-year-old center has reportedly expanded his list of acceptable destinations to 10 teams, giving Horcoff additional flexibility to evaluate potential offers. However, finding the right destination is only half the battle. Detroit must also convince another organization to surrender enough talent to justify losing one of its most important offensive players. As we previously reported , the Red Wings reportedly expressed concerns about Minnesota Wild prospect Danila Yurov serving as a centerpiece in a potential Larkin package. Frank Seravalli indicated that the two teams differed in their evaluations of the 22-year-old forward, creating another obstacle to a possible agreement. That situation illustrates why Friedman’s latest comments are particularly relevant. Detroit may be willing to consider younger assets, but that does not mean management intends to lower its standards regarding the quality of players coming back. If the Red Wings are going to sacrifice immediate production for future upside, they need to be confident that the player they acquire can eventually become a difference-maker. Otherwise, Detroit risks moving backward without obtaining the franchise-altering talent necessary to justify such a significant decision. Simon Edvinsson’s Situation Adds Another Layer The uncertainty surrounding Edvinsson makes Detroit’s reported interest in young centers even more intriguing. The 23-year-old defenseman remains unsigned, and his absence has created a substantial hole in the Red Wings’ lineup. Horcoff has repeatedly maintained that signing Edvinsson remains a priority, and he has publicly expressed no desire to trade him. As we previously reported , the Red Wings are willing to explore different contract structures in hopes of keeping their talented defenseman. Nevertheless, the ongoing stalemate has forced Detroit to consider what happens if an agreement cannot be reached. Edvinsson must sign a contract by December 1 to remain eligible to play in the NHL during the 2026-27 season. Moving Edvinsson could potentially give Detroit access to a young center that another organization would be unwilling to include in a Larkin trade. His combination of size, skating ability, and top-pair potential would make him an attractive asset for teams searching for a long-term solution on defense. Of course, that would create another significant problem for the Red Wings. Trading a 23-year-old defenseman with Edvinsson’s potential could leave Detroit searching for a replacement at one of the most difficult positions to fill. Apr 7, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson (77) passes in the first period against the Columbus Blue Jackets at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Are the Red Wings Preparing for Another Roster Reset? The bigger takeaway from Friedman’s reporting is that Detroit may be reconsidering how it wants to construct its next competitive team. For years, the organization has attempted to build around Larkin while developing young players who could eventually help return the Red Wings to the playoffs. Now, the uncertainty surrounding Larkin and Edvinsson has complicated that vision. Horcoff must determine whether acquiring established NHL contributors or investing in younger players provides the best opportunity for sustainable success. There is also an important distinction between preparing for a trade and committing to one. Detroit could be gathering information about young centers simply to understand its options while continuing to pursue resolutions that keep both Larkin and Edvinsson with the organization. Still, Friedman’s comments suggest rival general managers are beginning to understand exactly what Detroit values. If another team wants one of the Red Wings’ cornerstone players, offering the right young center could become the key to getting Horcoff’s attention. The Red Wings have already spent a decade trying to find their way back to the Stanley Cup Playoffs, and another prolonged rebuild would be difficult for fans to accept. But making a short-term move that leaves the organization worse off for years would be an even bigger mistake. For now, Detroit’s reported pursuit of young centers provides the clearest indication yet of the type of return Horcoff may be seeking. Whether that ultimately leads to a blockbuster trade involving Larkin or Edvinsson remains to be seen.

item.title: Liverpool must go 'full gas' despite injury issues, says Iraola
item.description: Andoni Iraola will not relent from his high-energy playing style (Glyn KIRK) Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said on Friday he will not ease off his high intensity demands despite suffering a series of injuries. The Reds are set to be without Dominik Szoboszlai, Jeremie Frimpong and Victor Munoz for the visit of Brighton on Sunday, while Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo have recently returned from injuries picked up on international duty. Iraola's high-energy style at Bournemouth reaped success which earned him the job at Anfield, but for the first time in his managerial career he is having to deal with the added toll of European football. "The way we want to play you cannot play 70 per cent," Iraola said at his pre-match press conference. "Imagine you don't have a right-winger on the bench, I will put someone as a right-winger. I prefer to do this than you save your energy so you have to last 90 minutes. "Give everything for 60 minutes, 65, 70, 72, then someone will do the 18, 35, whatever because we need to play full gas. "I would like to say we are good enough to play 70 percent and win games but it's not (the case). We have to play our very best because the teams we have in front of us are very good." Liverpool go into the weekend four points adrift of third-placed Brighton, who are the Premier League's top scorers with 23 goals in seven games. "I think they are doing incredibly well. They deserved all the praise they are getting and I think there is little doubt there. I think it's a team that is very well coached," Iraola said. "We have to be at our very best to beat Brighton because now they are with confidence. But I also see my team in a good place." Szoboszlai's return from injury was cut short in last weekend's victory at Brentford, but Iraola is hopeful the Hungarian will not be sidelined for long. "I don't think he's far, but he hasn't trained with the group still and also considering that we started him and he had to go out, we will probably take one or two days more than we would last week," said the Spaniard. "He's in a good place. Dom is already training outside alone and he's going to train with the group but he's not ready for this one." kca/iwd

item.title: Under-15s and under-17s eye Campeonato Paulista quarter-final spots
item.description: Under-15s and under-17s eye Campeonato Paulista quarter-final spots This Saturday (24), São Paulo’s Under-15 and Under-17 teams take to the field seeking a place in the quarterfinals of the Campeonato Paulista. The Under-15s will play first. After thrashing Guarani 5-0 in Cotia in the first leg of the round of 16, with goals from Juninho, Luisinho, Gilbert, Pietro and Yahgo, Vinícius dos Santos’s side will face their opponents at 9 a.m. at Estádio Brinco de Ouro da Princesa in Campinas, São Paulo state. Thanks to their first-leg advantage, the Tricolor can lose by up to four goals and still qualify. Next, at 11 a.m., the Under-17s will face I9 at CFA Laudo Natel in Cotia, São Paulo state. In the first leg, played at I9’s training ground in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo state, Alexandre Torrezan’s side won 4-0, with two goals from Kelvyn and one each from Nicolas Francisco and Brenno. The team will now look to secure qualification at home. The match will be broadcast exclusively on SPFC Play. Both teams head into these matches with strong records in the state championship. The Under-17s finished top of their group in both the first and second stages. In total, they recorded 12 wins, three draws and three defeats, scoring 57 goals and conceding 15. They then faced Meia Noite, winning the first leg 2-0 away before cruising to a 6-0 victory in the return leg in Cotia. The Under-15s also topped their group in both previous stages, recording 14 wins, three draws and just one defeat. The team scored 68 goals and conceded 10. In the third stage, they faced AA Flamengo, drawing the first leg 1-1 away and winning the return leg 3-0 in Cotia. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Who Skip Bayless thinks will win the NFC North following the Chicago Bears’ latest game
item.description: Photo by Steve Zak Photography/FilmMagic The Chicago Bears have won the joint-most games in the NFC North at the time of writing, but Skip Bayless is not backing them to win the division. In turn, they are one place below the currently 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and one above the Green Bay Packers, who are yet to take to the field in Week 7 (4-2). The Colts have had a mixed start to the season, sitting with a 2-4 record. Elsewhere in the NFC North this weekend, the Green Bay Packers will take on the Lions in what could prove to be a big game in the division. Should the Packers secure the victory, they will end Week 7 with the same record as the Bears. Social Media React to Jeremy Lin’s ESPN Regular-Season Commentary Debut Lin worked alongside play-by-play announcer Ryan Ruocco for the Nuggets-Thunder broadcast. item.title: Ian Poulter becomes latest high profile player to quit LIV Golf
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Team Europe's Ian Poulter celebrates after his team won the Ryder Cup Golf Tournament over Team USA, at Le Golf National. (is associated with: «Ian Poulter becomes latest high profile player to quit LIV Golf») Gareth Fuller/PA Wire/dpa Ian Poulter has become the latest big name to quit LIV Golf as the ailing breakaway league looks to relaunch this year. Poulter said it was a "tough decision" to leave but he would relish "the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests." England's Poulter is the second player this week to announce he is leaving the troubled tour, after Louis Oosthuizen announced his intention to return to the DP World Tour next year. LIV is attempting to relaunch in 2027 as LIV 2.0. with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support after ploughing in $5 billion over four years. In order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of all its existing players, clearly in the hope that they will re-sign on new terms. However, Poulter will not be among them. He insisted he had no regrets about moving to the rival tour, which split the sport down the middle and continues to cause friction between opposing players. The DP World Tour has confirmed it will be taking a tougher line and that any player signing with the new-look LIV will be ineligible for membership and therefore ruled out of Ryder Cup contention. Poulter added: "Clearly LIV Golf has divided opinion, but to be part of the founding group who took world class golf around the globe... is something I will be forever proud of. "Change is never easy and it's fair to say professional golf has experienced plenty of it over the last few years. But I've always believed that change can create opportunities and ultimately lead to positive outcomes."

item.title: Messi Drops 2 Goals To Crush D.C. United And End Streak
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Lionel Messi proved he is still the king of Major League Soccer just four days after hanging up his Argentina jersey. He scored two goals to lead Inter Miami to a crushing 4-0 victory over D.C. United on Saturday night. This win snaps a five-match winless streak and puts the team back in the hunt for a top playoff seed. The 39-year-old superstar is not slowing down. He now has 23 goals this season, leading the entire league by a wide margin. According to Fox Sports , this performance cements his case as the favorite to win a third straight MVP award. His return to form shows that his focus is now fully on winning another MLS Cup with Miami. A Dominant Start for New Coach Kily Inter Miami needed this win badly after a rough patch of four draws and one loss. Cristian “Kily” González, the new coach who assumed control in mid-September, celebrated his first league win with this victory. The team looked sharp from the start, with Luis Suárez scoring twice in the first half to build a 2-0 lead. Messi joined the party shortly after the break. He scored in the 47th minute after Suárez set him up with a simple pass. He added his second goal in the 60th minute with a brilliant solo effort. He dribbled past two defenders and beat the goalkeeper with a precise shot from 12 yards out. This display was a reminder of why he is the best player in the world. Why His Retirement Changes Everything Messi brought his curtain down on his Argentina career earlier this week in Buenos Aires. He scored his 126th and final goal for the country in a friendly match. Now, he has a contract with Miami through 2028, so his future is secure in Florida. His coach, Cristian “Kily” González, knows exactly how to handle this situation. “He’ll be missed in that jersey, of course, but today we have him here, and we have to enjoy having him with us now,” Kily said this week. The sentiment is simple: stop worrying about the past and watch him dominate the present. In 10 straight MLS games, he has already registered a goal contribution. Inter Miami now sits second in the Eastern Conference, just behind the leaders. They need a top-four seed to secure home-field advantage for the playoffs, which begin next month. With Messi contributing 13 assists and 23 goals, the team is well on its way to becoming the first to win back-to-back titles since 2011. The next test comes on Wednesday night when they host New York City FC.

item.description: Angelique S. Chengelis, Connor Earegood, John Niyo, and Bob Wojnowski of The Detroit News predict the outcome of Saturday's Michigan- Indiana game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor (Noon, Fox/94.7 FM) . ▶ Angelique S. item.description: Bruce Springsteen gave Brewers’ Pat Murphy special phone call before World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There’s no doubt that Pat Murphy loves Bruce Springsteen, and The Boss gave the manager a ring before the Milwaukee Brewers start the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. Murphy, who has a tattoo quoting the song “No Surrender” that reads, “No retreat, no surrender,” received a phone call from The Boss himself, as he told USA Today. He was getting a call from an unknown number that was trying to FaceTime him. However, upon looking at the area code (732), which is from Freehold, New Jersey, he knew who it was. They had a 10-minute chat that left Murphy “blown away,” though it’s exactly “what I expected” from a phone call with Springsteen. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It was as real as you can get,” the Brewers’ manager described, “like we knew each other.” As the Brewers returned home from Los Angeles after beating the Dodgers to secure their spot in the World Series, Murphy was alerted that The Boss had called the office asking for his number. He wanted to speak with the manager, but it didn’t happen when he expected. Instead, it happened early in the morning when his kids were still sleeping. Murphy couldn’t help but fanboy a little bit. He told The Boss how he’s inspired him throughout his life and how a “big night out” is listening to Springsteen on Broadway while eating at home. Luckily, he wasn’t starstruck or nervous talking to him. He explained, “I felt pretty normal. It’s like you knew him your whole life. I feel like I do know him because I know so much about him. It was just as real as always, just like you’d want it.” He wishes he could do it all over again. After all, his fandom dates back decades. Murphy drove in the pouring rain to see Springsteen’s River Tour in the ’80s. Now, the focus is on the Brewers winning the World Series. Springsteen didn’t say he was rooting for the Brewers. Murphy said, “he didn’t go that far.” He has a few chances to “Prove It All Night” to The Boss. Between them, Messi and Ronaldo ringfenced the prize between 2008 and 2017, winning five apiece. After Luka Modric's 2018 success, Messi won three more. It meant the Ballon d'Or became a battleground in the race to be considered the greatest player of all time. Both men are coming to the end now. Messi has retired from international football, while Ronaldo is raging against the dying of the light and the Portugal national team setup. CR7 is absent from the nominees list once again, while rumours that Messi was in line to present the main award this year demonstrated where he sat in the 2026 pecking order. He was never seen as a sure thing to make the grade at Tottenham, spending several spells of varying success on loan in England's lower leagues. There were suspicions of a "one-season wonder" when he belatedly made his Spurs breakthrough in 2014/15, but Kane kept scoring and never stopped – something that also applies to his England career after a debut goal just 79 seconds after coming off the bench against Lithuania in March 2015. Getty Images Since then, Kane has added unforeseen gears to his game, most notably his phenomenal range of passing from deeper positions on the field. Just check out his assist for Alphonso Davies against Arsenal this week. He also has one of continental Europe's best teams built around him. Historically, that sort of thing doesn't happened for English players. Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Kevin Keegan could claim that at Hamburg in the late 1970s and Jude Bellingham might end up laying claim to one of the great Real Madrid careers. But from a country that is considered soccer's homeland, Kane has put himself in rarefied company. After Matthew, Charlton, Keegan and Michael Owen, he would be only the fifth Englishman to lift the Ballon d'Or. Owen's unlikely win in 2001 came during a spell of 14 first-time winners in 15 years before Ronaldo and Messi started doing their relentless thing. Brazil great Ronaldo was the only man to repeat during that 1993 to 2007 period. But his 2025/26 is as good as any season from the Ballon d'Or's before times. Roberto Baggio in 1993, Hristo Stoichkov in 1994, Fabio Cannavaro in 2006 and Kaka in 2007. Harry Kane in 2026 can sit proudly in that company as a great of his era.

As Robinson noted, Godwin has made uncharacteristic drops. He is getting older, and his injuries have sapped some of his explosiveness. Emeka Egbuka dealt with turf toe in the offseason and has not been as efficient at the start of the regular season. Ted Hurst is a third-round rookie, and Jalen McMillan is on the IR. They are not getting enough from this group. With all of it combined, they have one of the worst passing attacks in the NFL . Mandatory Credit: William Howard-USA TODAY Sports As the Deacs get ready for opening night in a couple of weeks, the staff has picked up a commit from local 4-star power forward Jayon Connor NEWS: 4⭐️ Jayon Connor has committed to Wake Forest, he told @Rivals . ⁰⁰The 6-foot-7 forward is a top-100 recruit in the 2027 class. https://t.co/xwhtJUjkaj pic.twitter.com/fgAQnr0MXp — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) October 23, 2026 Connor is a 6-7 PF who plays right down the road at Forsyth Country Day. He is rated as a 4-star prospect and the 83rd best player in the 2027 class by 247Sports. He chose to stay in Winston Salem and play for the Deacs over competing offers from a ton of schools, including: Virginia Tech, Clemson, NC State, Georgia Tech, Houston, Illinois, Tennessee, Texas A&M, Vanderbilt, USC, and West Virginia. As a junior at Forsyth Country Day, Connor averaged 20 points, 9.4 rebounds, 1.9 steals, and 0.9 blocks per game. From the scouting reports, it seems like his biggest asset is his motor—despite being undersized for a power forward, his aggression and tenacity make him a formidable rebounder and defender. He is a player who doesn’t mind doing the dirty work or sacrificing his body to help the team. Offensively, Connor scored most of his points around the rim, either off of drives or offensive rebounds. His shooting is going to require some development—Connor shot just 2-18 (11%) from beyond the arc and 24-55 (44%) from the free throw line last season. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
